key_gap: Both sides produced the identical plan — ~20 vans + ~8 drivers (~$1.4M), drivers-not-vans as the binding pool (52 < 56 van-days, docks/pick free), the naive 2x-van proposal refuted with its own numbers (80 vans still deliver 52 x 50 x 6 = 15,600/wk < 16,800), and the norm-degradation margin with a re-measure point. The gap is epistemic stance: the human ran an explicit attack pass on the rebuild's load-bearing assumptions BEFORE finalizing — utilization-as-headroom (tested: half-right, rejected at pool level — idle van-hours need drivers), route-norm constancy (tested: partially succeeds — effective norm ~47 at volume → 2,800/47 ≈ 60 van-days, plan revised upward), union cap flexibility (tested: fails short-term) — and the falsification demonstrably CHANGED the rebuild. The AI reached the same margin via a post-selection premortem + contract check: it verified the selected option instead of attempting the hardest attacks on the model, treated the utilization trap as an evidence-hierarchy point rather than a tested hypothesis, and paid alternatives-generation + verification overhead to arrive at what the human landed first-pass.
learning_signal: The combo's value is that falsification runs BEFORE the conclusion is fixed, and the double pass earns its cost when the hardest attack changes the rebuild. To adopt it: (1) after building the leading model, enumerate its load-bearing assumptions explicitly (for a constraint problem: which pool binds, is the output norm stable at volume, are the caps enforceable) and attempt the strongest counter-claim against EACH with a tested outcome — record the verdict and the surviving revision; (2) treat 'falsification of the leading model' as a pre-decision gate, not a REVIEW activity — a post-selection premortem is verification, and it misses the case where the model itself is wrong in a way the selected alternative inherits; (3) when utilization/headroom evidence appears (X% idle, Y% spare), force a constraint-pool enumeration — utilization at one resource level is not dispatchable capacity when a different pool (drivers, licenses, floor space) binds; (4) let a partially-successful attack revise the plan upward rather than discard it — the falsification outcome that added the norm-degradation margin (20 vans + 8 drivers vs bare 16 + 4) is the deliverable's best part; (5) state what would revise the plan (re-measure the effective norm at the new load, contract window opening) so the falsification loop continues after the decision.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'hardest-attack pass' to the WHY→HOW boundary: after the leading hypothesis is formed, (a) require an explicit enumeration of its load-bearing assumptions; (b) for each, generate the strongest counter-claim and test it against the data, recording the verdict (rejected / partially-succeeds / succeeds) — the HOW alternative set should include the surviving revisions, not just the pre-existing options; (c) when utilization or headroom evidence is present, force a constraint-pool enumeration in WHY (the binding pool may not be the idle resource); (d) route the falsification outcomes into the decision packet as a dedicated evidence line ('assumption attacked / outcome / revision') so the model-change provenance is auditable; (e) efficiency guard: budget the attack pass to the decision's stakes so the double pass does not double the work on low-stakes items.

key_gap: The pure style executed its signature double pass and failed on it: the rebuild re-derived the profit arithmetic correctly (5,000 x $3 - $12,000 = $3,000; 5,750 x $2.20 - $12,000 = $650, -$2,350/-78%), and the falsification pass then attacked the rebuild's assumptions — COGS flex (narrows the loss to -$50), elasticity (cut only breaks even at elasticity >= 3.6), fixed-cost stability (needs data not supplied) — and each attack was internally sound but aimed OUTSIDE the request's scope. The inputs WERE the model: there was no hypothesis to rebuild and nothing falsifiable to break; the pass manufactured uncertainty, converted a direct computation into 'it depends on elasticity,' and blew the 5-minute deadline — the CFO walked into the call with a conditional instead of a number. The AI won on scope containment: META sized the effort E1 with TIME as the binding constraint, WHAT declared the scope closed (elasticity/cost-curve analysis explicitly not asked for), WHY found no missing evidence and VOI <= cost (even at elasticity 2 the cut still loses, $1,200 < $3,000 — the given-numbers verdict is robust), HOW rejected the sensitivity-model alternative on scope + deadline + robustness grounds, and the packet delivered the number, the yes/no, and a one-line deferral of the sensitivity question.
learning_signal: The double pass has no target when the request is a closed-scope computation — 'rebuild from fundamentals' collapses to the computation itself and 'falsify hardest' manufactures scope; the failure is converting an arithmetic ask into a conditional, not any error in the math. The correct discipline: (1) in framing, detect closed-scope requests — all decision variables supplied, deliverable is a computation, explicit deadline — and budget effort accordingly (E1, time = the constraint); (2) treat supplied assumptions as the model, not parameters to model: the given 15% volume estimate is the input to test, and a sensitivity model that needs data the requester did not supply is scope-creep; (3) before any falsification pass, ask 'is there a load-bearing claim here that the answer depends on?' — for a direct computation the answer is no, and the pass is waste; (4) use robustness, not sensitivity, for the deadline: the given-numbers verdict held at elasticity 2 (still -$1,800/month), so the go/no-go was robust and the answer was ready in the first model pass; (5) defer, don't smuggle: state the open questions (real elasticity, COGS flex) as a one-line follow-up in the packet — the CFO can commission them after the call; scope discipline is not a substitute for flagging them.
suggested_improvement: Add a 'closed-scope fast path' to META/WHAT: (a) in META, if the task signature is closed-scope (inputs complete, deliverable is a computation, hard deadline, stakes low-medium), set effort E1 and declare the deadline the binding constraint; (b) in WHAT, add an explicit 'is this request closed-scope?' check that closes the WHY/HOW deepen-reflex — no rebuild pass and no falsification pass when the inputs ARE the model (G-WHY-4 VOI <= cost should fire and terminate diagnosis); (c) in HOW, evaluate any 'add a model/sensitivity analysis' alternative against scope + deadline + robustness BEFORE generating it fully — if the given-numbers verdict is robust to plausible variation, reject it and state the robustness bound in one line; (d) require a 'deferred questions' line in every decision packet so scope containment never looks like the open questions were missed; (e) guard the other direction: the same fast path must explicitly re-open when the request is contested-input or open-scope (a flag in the packet), so scope discipline does not suppress a needed sensitivity check.
